title: 10.3 Small Group · Group 1
contentObjective: With my small group, I can use patterns and relationships to make sense of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle and think logically about its solutions — one step at a time, with support.
languageObjective: I can talk through each step out loud using a sentence frame and the lesson's key words.

turnAndTalk.question: A one-disc Tower of Hanoi takes 1 move, a two-disc tower takes 3 moves, and a three-disc tower takes 7 moves. What pattern rule takes you from one row to the next?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The pattern rule is to double the previous number of moves and add 1: 1 × 2 + 1 = 3, and 3 × 2 + 1 = 7.

launch.narrative: This is your support small group for Lesson 10.3. We're going to slow this down and build it together, one step at a time. You can ask a question any time — that's what this group is for.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — Playing with math means playing with patterns
conceptIntro.intro: The objective is to move the whole stack of discs to another rod. The rules: move only one disc at a time, move only the top disc from a stack, and never place a larger disc on top of a smaller disc. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: We play with math by using our imagination and by looking for patterns or relationships that help us think logically — a pattern can tell us the answer to a puzzle we have not even played yet.

iDo.title: Watch me imagine the solution first
lines: Before moving anything, I describe what the solved puzzle will look like: the discs in the same order — smallest on top to largest on bottom — but on a different rod.
Then I play the small cases: a one-disc tower takes 1 move, and a two-disc tower takes 3 moves.
A three-disc tower takes at least 7 moves. Small cases are how mathematicians play.

weDo.title: Let's organize the moves in a table
lines: Discs: 1, 2, 3 — Steps: 1, 3, 7. What is happening from each row to the next?
Double the number of steps and add 1: 1 doubled plus 1 is 3, and 3 doubled plus 1 is 7.
So 4 discs take 7 × 2 + 1 = 15 steps, and 5 discs take 15 × 2 + 1 = 31 steps.
The pattern just solved a puzzle we never touched.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "My first step is ___ , because the problem asks for ___ ."

youDo.title: Now you try — with support
lines: Try the practice problems below. The hint button is right there whenever you get stuck — use it, that's smart.

Remember the key idea: We play with math by using our imagination and by looking for patterns or relationships that help us think logically — a pattern can tell us the answer to a puzzle we have not even played yet..

connect.scenario: You solved the small towers by hand: 1 disc takes 1 step, 2 discs take 3 steps, 3 discs take 7 steps. Now someone hands you a five-disc tower and asks for the fewest steps — but you do not have time to play it out.
connect.promptQuestion: How can a pattern help you imagine the solution?
connect.prompt: The pattern rule for the Tower of Hanoi is to ___ the number of steps for the smaller tower and ___ for each new disc. Applying this rule twice starting from 7 steps for a three-disc tower gives a five-disc tower a minimum of ___ steps.

check.stem: The table shows: 1 disc = 1 step, 2 discs = 3 steps, 3 discs = 7 steps. What is the pattern rule from one row to the next?
choices: Add 2 to the previous number of steps
Double the previous number of steps and add 1
Multiply the previous number of steps by 3
Add the disc number to the previous steps
check.explanation: 1 × 2 + 1 = 3 and 3 × 2 + 1 = 7, so the rule is double and add 1. Adding 2 matches 1→3 but fails on 3→5≠7, multiplying by 3 matches 1→3 but fails on 3→9≠7, and adding the disc number matches 1+2=3 but fails on 3+3=6≠7.

check.stem: Using the rule "double the steps and add 1," how many steps does a 4-disc tower take, starting from the 3-disc value of 7 steps?
check.explanation: 7 × 2 + 1 = 15. 8 comes from only adding 1 without doubling, 14 comes from only doubling without adding 1, and 21 comes from tripling instead of doubling.

check.stem: Continuing the pattern from 15 steps for a 4-disc tower, how many steps does a 5-disc tower take?
check.explanation: 15 × 2 + 1 = 31. 16 comes from only adding 1, 30 comes from only doubling, and 45 comes from tripling 15 instead of doubling and adding 1.

connect.modelAnswer: I would organize what I know in a table: 1 disc takes 1 step, 2 discs take 3, 3 discs take 7. The pattern rule is to double the number of steps and add 1 for each new disc. So 4 discs take 7 × 2 + 1 = 15 steps, and 5 discs take 15 × 2 + 1 = 31 steps. The pattern let me imagine the solution — a minimum of 31 steps — without ever touching the discs.

diagram.title: Fewest Moves in Tower of Hanoi
diagram.caption: Each bar doubles the one before it and adds 1: 1, 3, 7, 15, 31. One more disc nearly doubles the work, so the bars grow far faster than the disc count.

approaching.stem: What is the fewest number of moves needed to solve a three-disc Tower of Hanoi puzzle?
choices: 7 moves
3 moves
6 moves
9 moves
approaching.explanation: It takes at least 7 moves to solve a three-disc Tower of Hanoi puzzle.
choiceFeedback: 3 is the number of DISCS — moving each disc only once is impossible because of the size rule.
6 doubles the 3 discs but forgets the extra move — the pattern is double and add 1, so 3 discs need 7.
9 is 3 × 3, but the fewest-moves count follows the doubling pattern, not disc × disc.
hints: It is more than one move per disc.
A two-disc tower already takes 3 moves.
Double 3 and add 1.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el menor número de movimientos necesarios para resolver la Torre de Hanói de tres discos?
approaching.explanationEs: Se necesitan al menos 7 movimientos para resolver la Torre de Hanói de tres discos.
hintsEs: Es más de un movimiento por disco.
Una torre de dos discos ya toma 3 movimientos.
Duplica 3 y suma 1.

approaching.stem: Which move is against the rules of the Tower of Hanoi?
choices: Placing a larger disc on top of a smaller disc
Moving one disc at a time
Moving the top disc from a stack
Placing a smaller disc on top of a larger disc
approaching.explanation: A larger disc can never be on top of a smaller disc — that is the rule that makes the puzzle a puzzle.
choiceFeedback: One disc at a time is exactly what the rules require, not what they forbid.
You may only move the TOP disc of a stack — that move follows the rules.
Smaller on top of larger is the legal direction; it is the reverse that is banned.
hints: Two of these are the rules themselves.
Think about disc SIZES.
Which stacking order would crush a smaller disc?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál movimiento va contra las reglas de la Torre de Hanói?
approaching.explanationEs: Un disco más grande nunca puede estar sobre uno más pequeño — esa es la regla que hace que el rompecabezas sea un rompecabezas.
hintsEs: Dos de estas son las reglas mismas.
Piensa en los TAMAÑOS de los discos.
¿Cuál orden de apilado aplastaría un disco más pequeño?
choicesEs: Poner un disco más grande sobre uno más pequeño
Mover un disco a la vez

approaching.stem: What will the solved puzzle look like?
choices: The discs in the same order — smallest on top to largest on bottom — but on a different rod
The discs in reverse order, largest on top
The discs spread out with one disc on each rod
The discs back on the starting rod in any order
approaching.explanation: The goal is to rebuild the whole stack, smallest to largest, on a different rod.
choiceFeedback: Largest on top would break the rule — a larger disc can never sit on a smaller one.
Spreading the discs out is a middle step, not the finished puzzle.
The stack must END on a different rod, and the size order is required, not optional.
hints: Imagine the ending before you start.
The stack looks just like the start.
Only its rod has changed.
approaching.explanationEs: La meta es reconstruir toda la pila, del más pequeño al más grande, en otra varilla.
hintsEs: Imagina el final antes de empezar.
La pila se ve igual que al inicio.
Solo cambió su varilla.
choicesEs: Los discos en el mismo orden — el más pequeño arriba y el más grande abajo — pero en otra varilla
Los discos en orden inverso, el más grande arriba
Los discos repartidos con un disco en cada varilla
Los discos de vuelta en la varilla inicial en cualquier orden

approaching.stem: How many moves does a one-disc tower take? A two-disc tower?
choices: 1 move and 3 moves
1 move and 2 moves
2 moves and 4 moves
1 move and 4 moves
approaching.explanation: You can solve a one-disc tower in 1 step and a two-disc tower in 3 steps.
choiceFeedback: 2 moves is not enough for two discs — the small disc must move aside, the large disc moves, then the small disc moves back on top: 3 moves.
One disc needs only 1 move — just lift it to another rod.
4 moves is one too many for two discs — the fewest is 3.
hints: Play the one-disc game in your head first.
For two discs: the small one has to get out of the way, and later get back on top.
Count those three separate moves.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuántos movimientos toma una torre de un disco? ¿Y una de dos discos?
approaching.explanationEs: Puedes resolver una torre de un disco en 1 paso y una de dos discos en 3 pasos.
hintsEs: Juega primero en tu mente el juego de un disco.
Para dos discos: el pequeño tiene que quitarse del camino y después volver arriba.
Cuenta esos tres movimientos por separado.

approaching.instructions: Sort each move: is it allowed by the Tower of Hanoi rules, or against them?
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada movimiento: ¿lo permiten las reglas de la Torre de Hanói o va en contra de ellas?
approaching.label: Sort each move: legal or against the rules?
approaching.labelEs: Clasifica cada movimiento: ¿legal o contra las reglas?

categories.label: Legal move
items: Move the top disc of any stack
Place a small disc on a bigger disc
Move exactly one disc at a time
itemsEs: Mover el disco de arriba de cualquier pila
Colocar un disco pequeño sobre uno más grande
Mover exactamente un disco a la vez

categories.label: Against the rules
items: Place a big disc on a smaller disc
Pull a disc out from the middle of a stack
itemsEs: Mover dos discos a la vez
Colocar un disco grande sobre uno más pequeño
Sacar un disco de en medio de una pila

hints: Only the TOP disc of a stack can move, and only one at a time.
The size rule: smaller may rest on bigger, never the reverse.
hintsEs: Solo el disco de ARRIBA de una pila puede moverse, y solo uno a la vez.
La regla del tamaño: el pequeño puede descansar sobre el grande, nunca al revés.
approaching.explanation: The three legal moves are the whole rule set: take only a top disc, move one at a time, and rest smaller on bigger. The illegal moves each break exactly one rule — two at once, big on small, or grabbing from mid-stack. Every 2ⁿ − 1 solution is built from nothing but the legal three.
approaching.explanationEs: Los tres movimientos legales son todo el reglamento: tomar solo el disco de arriba, mover uno a la vez y apoyar el pequeño sobre el grande. Los ilegales rompen exactamente una regla cada uno: dos a la vez, grande sobre pequeño o sacar de en medio. Cada solución de 2ⁿ − 1 se construye solo con los tres legales.

approaching.label: Use the doubling pattern to complete the table of fewest moves.
approaching.labelEs: Usa el patrón de duplicación para completar la tabla de movimientos mínimos.
hints: Each new disc means: solve the smaller tower, move the big disc, solve the smaller tower again.
That is why the rule is double-plus-one: two copies of the previous answer, plus one move for the biggest disc.
hintsEs: Cada disco nuevo significa: resolver la torre más pequeña, mover el disco grande y resolver la torre pequeña otra vez.
Por eso la regla es duplicar y sumar uno: dos copias de la respuesta anterior más un movimiento para el disco más grande.
approaching.explanation: The recursion is the reason for the rule: to move n discs you solve n − 1 discs (7 moves), carry the biggest disc (1 move), and solve n − 1 again (7 moves) — so 4 discs need 15, 5 need 31, and 6 need 2 × 31 + 1 = 63. The pattern 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63 is one less than the doubling numbers 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64.
approaching.explanationEs: La recursión explica la regla: para mover n discos resuelves n − 1 discos (7 movimientos), llevas el disco más grande (1 movimiento) y resuelves n − 1 otra vez (7 movimientos); por eso 4 discos necesitan 15, 5 necesitan 31 y 6 necesitan 2 × 31 + 1 = 63. El patrón 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63 es uno menos que los números que se duplican: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64.

onLevel.stem: The number of discs in a Tower of Hanoi puzzle can vary. What NEVER varies?
onLevel.modelAnswer: The number of rods never varies — there are always three rods, no matter how many discs the puzzle uses.

onLevel.stem: What does it mean to be playful with math? Use the Tower of Hanoi as your example.
onLevel.modelAnswer: Being playful with math means treating a problem like a game — imagining what the solution will look like, trying small cases, and hunting for a pattern. With the Tower of Hanoi, I played the one-disc and two-disc towers first, and the pattern I found told me about towers I never played.

onLevel.stem: The table shows 1 disc → 1 step, 2 discs → 3 steps, 3 discs → 7 steps. What is the pattern rule for the number of steps when you add one more disc?
choices: Double the number of steps and add 1
Add 2 to the number of steps
Add the number of discs to the steps
Multiply the number of steps by 3
onLevel.explanation: 1 × 2 + 1 = 3 and 3 × 2 + 1 = 7, so each new disc doubles the steps and adds 1.
choiceFeedback: Adding 2 fits 1 → 3 but fails the next row: 3 + 2 = 5, and the table says 7.
Adding the discs fits 1 → 3 (1 + 2) but fails the next row: 3 + 3 = 6, and the table says 7.
Multiplying by 3 fits 1 → 3 but fails the next row: 3 × 3 = 9, and the table says 7.
hints: Test each rule on BOTH jumps: 1 → 3 and 3 → 7.
Several rules pass the first jump; only one passes both.
What do you do to 3 to land exactly on 7?
onLevel.stemEs: La tabla muestra 1 disco → 1 paso, 2 discos → 3 pasos, 3 discos → 7 pasos. ¿Cuál es la regla del patrón para el número de pasos cuando agregas un disco más?
onLevel.explanationEs: 1 × 2 + 1 = 3 y 3 × 2 + 1 = 7, así que cada disco nuevo duplica los pasos y suma 1.
hintsEs: Prueba cada regla en LOS DOS saltos: 1 → 3 y 3 → 7.
Varias reglas pasan el primer salto; solo una pasa los dos.
¿Qué le haces al 3 para caer exactamente en 7?
choicesEs: Duplicar el número de pasos y sumar 1
Suma el número de discos a los pasos
Multiplicar el número de pasos por 3

onLevel.stem: Use the pattern rule to complete the table: how many steps for a four-disc tower?
choices: 15 steps
14 steps
9 steps
28 steps
onLevel.explanation: A three-disc tower takes 7 steps, so a four-disc tower takes 7 × 2 + 1 = 15 steps.
choiceFeedback: 14 doubles the 7 steps but forgets to add 1.
9 adds 2 to 7 instead of doubling and adding 1.
28 multiplies 7 by 4 (the number of discs) instead of doubling once and adding 1.
hints: Start from the three-disc answer: 7 steps.
Apply the rule: double, then add 1.
onLevel.stemEs: Usa la regla del patrón para completar la tabla: ¿cuántos pasos para una torre de cuatro discos?
onLevel.explanationEs: Una torre de tres discos toma 7 pasos, así que una torre de cuatro discos toma 7 × 2 + 1 = 15 pasos.
hintsEs: Empieza con la respuesta de tres discos: 7 pasos.
Aplica la regla: duplica y luego suma 1.

onLevel.stem: What is the minimum number of steps to solve a FIVE-disc Tower of Hanoi puzzle?
choices: 31 steps
15 steps
30 steps
35 steps
onLevel.explanation: A four-disc tower takes 15 steps, so a five-disc tower takes 15 × 2 + 1 = 31 steps.
choiceFeedback: 15 steps is the answer for FOUR discs — the fifth disc requires applying the rule once more.
30 doubles the 15 steps but forgets to add 1.
35 adds 5 discs × 4 to 15 — the rule is double and add 1, not add a multiple of the discs.
hints: You need the four-disc answer first: 15.
Apply the rule one more time.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el número mínimo de pasos para resolver la Torre de Hanói de CINCO discos?
onLevel.explanationEs: Una torre de cuatro discos toma 15 pasos, así que una torre de cinco discos toma 15 × 2 + 1 = 31 pasos.
hintsEs: Necesitas primero la respuesta de cuatro discos: 15.
Aplica la regla una vez más.

onLevel.stem: How can you ORGANIZE the information about discs and moves to help you see patterns?
onLevel.modelAnswer: I can create a table with one column for the number of discs and one for the number of steps: 1 and 1, 2 and 3, 3 and 7, 4 and 15, 5 and 31. With the numbers lined up in rows, I can compare each row to the next and spot the double-and-add-1 pattern.

onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cómo puedes ORGANIZAR la información sobre discos y movimientos para ayudarte a ver patrones?

practice.commonMistake: Doubling the previous number of steps but forgetting to add 1 — answering 14 instead of 15 for four discs, or 30 instead of 31 for five.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explanation: A square folds onto itself along both diagonals and both midlines — 4 lines in all.

questions.stem: A shape has bilateral symmetry. This means…
choices: one line splits it into two mirror halves
it has four equal sides
it can be turned in a circle
it has no straight edges
questions.explanation: Bilateral symmetry means a single line divides the shape into halves that mirror each other.

questions.stem: Which capital letter has a vertical line of symmetry?
choices: A
R
P
F
questions.explanation: A folds onto itself along a vertical line down its middle. R, P and F do not.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon has 6 lines of symmetry — one through each pair of opposite vertices and each pair of opposite sides.
